newsitem.title: USA: FULL TEXT - Walt Disney Co Q2 earnings.
newsitem.headline: FULL TEXT - Walt Disney Co Q2 earnings.

text.p: Walt Disney Co released second quarter earnings per share of $0.49, beating Wall Street analysts' estimates of $0.45 a share compared to earnings last year of $0.33 a share.
The results were led by record attendance levels with a 14 percent jump in revenues at Disney's theme parks and resorts.
Total Revenues jumped to $5.48 billion from $4.54 billion.
The following is the full text release of the company's earnings announcement.

BURBANK, Calif., April 23 - The Walt Disney Company today reported significant increases in revenues, operating income, net income and earnings per share for both the second quarter and six months ended March 31, 1997.

On a pro forma basis and excluding the non-recurring items discussed below, revenues for the quarter increased 10% to $5.5 billion and operating income increased 32% to $864 million. Net income for the quarter increased 63% to $333 million and earnings per share increased 63% to $0.49. Revenues for the six-month period increased 8% to $11.8 billion and operating income increased 24% to $2.3 billion. Net income for the six months increased 31% to $1.0 billion and earnings per share increased 32% to $1.46.

"I am extremely pleased with Disney's outstanding results for the quarter which reflect strong profit growth for the Company," said Michael D. Eisner, chairman and CEO. "The performance of our Creative Content segment included impressive box office results from our most recent theatrical releases, including the Academy Award winning The English Patient,' and continued growth in worldwide merchandise licensing. Our Theme Park business continues to deliver excellent results with record attendance levels, led by Walt Disney World which is celebrating its 25th Anniversary. Strong performance from ESPN was also a significant factor in the Company's overall results."

In the prior year, the Company acquired the operations of ABC. Accordingly, the Company's results for the prior-year quarter and six-month period on an as reported basis do not fully reflect the acquisition, which became effective on February 9, 1996. To enhance comparability, the operating results for the quarter and six months ended March 31, 1996 are presented and discussed on a pro forma basis, which assumes the acquisition of ABC occurred at the beginning of such periods. In addition, the discussion of the Company's operating results excludes the impact of two non-recurring charges recorded by the Company during the second quarter of the prior year as well as the gain on the sale of KCAL recorded by the Company in the first quarter of the current year. Both the prior-year non-recurring items and the gain on the sale of KCAL are discussed below.

Creative Content revenues for the quarter increased 9% to $2.8 billion and operating income increased 56% to $390 million. For the six-month period, revenues increased 7% to $6.0 billion and operating income increased 23% to $1.1 billion.

Creative content results for the quarter and six months reflected the worldwide theatrical performance of "Ransom," "101 Dalmatians" and "The English Patient," and the home video success of "Toy Story" and "The Hunchback of Notre Dame" worldwide and "Bambi" domestically. Both periods reflected growth in the distribution of theatrical releases in the international television market and the continued growth in worldwide character merchandise licensing, including "Winnie the Pooh" and "101 Dalmatians." The results for the quarter also reflected the successful domestic releases of "Evita" and "Jungle 2 Jungle." In addition, the prior-year second quarter results reflected the write-off of certain development projects.

Broadcasting revenues for the quarter increased 9% to $1.5 billion and operating income increased 18% to $238 million. For the six-month period, revenues increased 6% to $3.4 billion and operating income increased 31% to $716 million.

Broadcasting results for the quarter and six months benefited from significant reductions in program amortization and other costs attributable to the acquisition, primarily at the television network, which were partially offset by lower network ratings. The quarter and six months also reflected strong cable results driven by increased advertising revenues and subscribers at ESPN and increased subscribers at The Disney Channel. The six-month period also reflected increased political advertising revenues at the owned TV stations.
